item.title: Definition of an Integral Domain
item.description: If we have a commutative ring with unity R, then R is an integral domain if it has no zero divisors (e.g. \mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{R}, and \mathbb{C}): Commutative, Unity is 1, a \cdot b=0\iff a=0\text{ or }b=0.
